cpu_capabilities.model: Intel(R) Xeon(R) CPU E3-1245 V2 @ 3.40GHz (Ivy Bridge, family 6 model 58)
cpu_capabilities.summary: Supports 128-bit SSE2/SSE4.1 (4-wide f32 and 4-wide u32/i32) AND 256-bit AVX1 floating-point (8-wide f32: vaddps/vsubps/vmulps/vdivps/vsqrtps/vcmpps/vblendvps). Does NOT support 256-bit integer AVX2 or FMA.

c_baseline: gcc-10 -O2 -ffp-contract=off (direct paired runs on CPU 7, 1 thread; gcc-10 -O2 does not auto-vectorize by default)
measurement_note: Every SIMD variant patches only the hot loop symbol inside the unmodified bend5k_o2 -O2 binary (same Bend5k runtime, same +RTS --threads 1 --gpu off -RTS flags) via intra-module call redirection. All timings are 5-run medians on CPU 7 with exact bit-identical stdout checksums verified against gcc-10 -O2.

probes.benchmark: bench/runtime/nbody/main.bend (scaled SY=14n, ST=300n; 131,072 3-body systems x 300 symplectic Euler steps)

variants.name: a_sse2_4wide_chunk
variants.note: CRUSHES gcc-10 -O2 BY 3.91x (0.256x C, 3.768x speedup vs scalar bend5k)! Replaces $direct.chunk (8 independent systems per fork leaf) with 2 batches of 4-wide SSE2 (addps/subps/mulps/sqrtps/divps) across 4 systems simultaneously, then tail-calls $direct.chunk(j=0) for exact Bend5k Hl{} heap return. Because scalar nbody is 100% latency/throughput-bound on sqrtss+divss, 4-wide SSE2 achieves near-ideal 3.77x scaling with bit-identical IEEE-754 f32 results.

variants.name: b_avx1_8wide_chunk
variants.note: 5.44x FASTER THAN gcc-10 -O2 (0.184x C, 5.247x speedup vs scalar bend5k)! Runs ALL 8 systems of $direct.chunk in a single 8-wide 256-bit AVX1 pass (vaddps/vsubps/vmulps/vsqrtps/vdivps; valid on Ivy Bridge since AVX1 supports 256-bit FP!). Pure 1-core FP SIMD ceiling.

probes.verdict: STRONG GO (4-wide SSE2 hits 0.256x C [3.91x faster than C] using only 5 packed FP ops that elf.bend already encodes with a 0xF3 drop; optional 8-wide AVX1 VEX hits 0.184x C [5.44x faster than C]!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~95 LOC (~10 LOC elf.bend packed addps/subps/mulps/divps/sqrtps + movups, ~85 LOC fork-leaf V4 kernel cloning for counted leaf loops like chunk(8n))

probes.benchmark: bench/runtime/kmeans/main.bend (scaled SIZE=13n; 64 restarts x 20 rounds x 8,192 points x K=8 centroids)

variants.name: a_sse2_k8_centroids_pmaddwd
variants.note: PURE SSE2 BEATS gcc-10 -O2 BY 1.80x (0.554x C, 2.957x speedup vs scalar bend5k) while KEEPING Bend5k's exact unmodified 15-node St tree + szip merge! Packs c0..c3 and c4..c7 (already (cy<<16)|cx = 8x i16!) into two XMM regs; per point, psubw + pmaddwd computes dx^2+dy^2 for 4 centroids in 2 pure SSE2 insns (|dx|,|dy|<=1023, exact signed 16-bit), followed by pslld/por/pcmpgtd/pshufd argmin and indexed sx/sy/sn update.

variants.name: b_sse41_k8_plus_simd_prng
variants.note: Adds SSE4.1 pminud + 4-wide SIMD PRNG (pmulld/pslld/psrld/pxor) inside $direct.chunk while still materializing Bend5k's St tree per 64-pt chunk (163,840 chunks x 15 St nodes + szip merges = ~115 ms of tree alloc/merge overhead remaining).

variants.name: c_sse41_k8_plus_flat_pfold
variants.note: CRUSHES gcc-10 -O2 BY 4.68x (0.214x C against paired 353.37 ms C run [raw 356.3, 350.4, 354.12, 349.74, 353.37]; 7.688x speedup vs scalar bend5k)! Deforesting pfold's recursive szip tree into a flat 24-scalar accumulator loop + our K=8 SSE2/SSE4.1 centroid distance kernel eliminates 99.6% of St heap allocations (1 St tree per Lloyd round instead of 255) and hits 75.50 ms!

probes.verdict: STRONG GO (pure SSE2 K=8 centroids alone hits 0.554x C [2.96x vs base]; combining with pfold tree-deforestation hits 0.214x C [4.68x faster than C, 7.69x vs base]!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~110 LOC (~30 LOC elf.bend SSE2/SSE4.1 integer ops [psubw/pmaddwd/paddd/pslld/por/pcmpgtd/pshufd/pminud/pmulld], ~80 LOC SLP K-way horizontal distance-min vectorization + indexed bucket accum)

probes.benchmark: bench/runtime/raytrace/main.bend (scaled ROWS=8, WIDTH=1000, DEPTH=4; 256 x 1000 pixels x 4 supersampled sub-rays x up to 5 bounces x 9 spheres)

variants.name: a_sse2_4wide_spheres
variants.note: 4-wide SSE2 across spheres (0..3, 4..7 + scalar 8) in nearest/nearest.t + unboxed trace bounce loop. Beats gcc-10 -O2 by 1.54x (0.648x C), but leaves subray/trace shading (sqrt + 7 divss) scalar and pays horizontal sphere-index extraction on every hit.

variants.name: b_avx1_8wide_spheres
variants.note: 8-wide AVX1 across spheres 0..7 in a single vsqrtps + scalar sphere 8. Only 3.4 ms faster than 4-wide spheres because scalar shading + horizontal extraction dominate once nearest is vectorized.

variants.name: c_sse2_4wide_subpixels
variants.note: OBLITERATES gcc-10 -O2 BY 3.86x (0.259x C, 8.169x speedup vs scalar bend5k, 2.5x faster than sphere-SIMD)! Vectorizing the 4 supersampled sub-pixels (l1..l4 in pixel) in 4-wide SSE2 runs EVERY sqrt and div (primary ray norm, nearest isect, light distance, normal/light norm, shadow isect) 4-wide with zero horizontal reduction and high spatial coherence across the 2x2 sub-pixel quad! Projects FULL raytrace (ROWS=12, WIDTH=6000) to ~4.9s (vs ~19s C)!

probes.verdict: STRONG GO (4-wide SSE2 across the 4 supersampled sub-pixels hits 0.259x C [3.86x faster than C, 8.17x vs base] — strictly dominates sphere-level SIMD [0.648x C] because it vectorizes 100% of subray + trace + nearest + nearest.t under the same fork-leaf V4 batching pass as nbody!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~90 LOC (reuses nbody's fork-leaf V4 FP cloning + ~25 LOC elf.bend cmpps/andps/andnps/orps/movmskps predicated select & active-lane mask)

probes.benchmark: bench/runtime/terrain/main.bend (scaled SIZE=13n, EPASS=5n; 8,192 independent 64x64 tiles x [fill + 5 Gauss-Seidel erode sweeps + 64-bin hist])

variants.name: a_sse41_intratile_fill_rough
variants.note: Intra-tile 4-wide SSE4.1 (4-wide ground() fill + 4-wide rough PRNG in erode, flat u32[4096] stack tile, scalar Gauss-Seidel erode stencil) hits 689.27 ms vs paired 989.96 ms C (0.696x C). Limited by the 5 Gauss-Seidel erode passes whose h[i] <- h[i-1] horizontal loop-carried dependency prevents intra-row vectorization.

variants.name: b_sse41_4wide_cross_tile_batch
variants.note: CRUSHES gcc-10 -O2 BY 4.07x (0.245x C, 7.047x speedup vs scalar bend5k, 2.83x faster than intra-tile SIMD)! Batching 4 independent fork-tree leaves in batch(d=2) with SoA tile layout (__m128i h[4096]) eliminates the Gauss-Seidel cross-lane dependency completely and vectorizes 100% of fill AND 100% of all 5 erode sweeps in 4-wide SSE4.1 (paddd/psubd/pslld/psrld/pand/pxor/pmulld)! Projects FULL terrain (SIZE=16n) from 13.6s down to ~1.95s (vs 7.87s C)!

probes.verdict: STRONG GO (cross-tile 4-wide SSE4.1 fork-leaf batching hits 0.245x C [4.07x faster than C, 7.05x vs base] — same unified fork-leaf V4 batching pass as nbody & raytrace, proving that Bend's fork-tree parallelism maps directly onto 1-core SIMD lanes!)
probes.estimated_loc: ~65 LOC (reuses the same fork-leaf V4 cloning + SoA stack-array promotion [U32*N] -> [V4U32*N] + shared SSE2/SSE4.1 integer opcodes from kmeans)

wave13_simd_design.core_insight: ALL FOUR benchmarks break <= 0.26x C (3.86x-5.44x faster than gcc-10 -O2 on 1 core!) via ONE unified Bend4 IR pattern: Fork-Leaf / Uniform-Call 4-Wide SIMD Batching (nbody chunk(8n), raytrace pixel 4x subray, terrain batch(d=2) 4x tile) plus K-way SLP horizontal vectorization for kmeans.

new_sse2_fp_5_plus_6_ops: addps (0F 58), subps (0F 5C), mulps (0F 59), divps (0F 5E), sqrtps (0F 51) -- literally omit 0xF3 in elf_emit_xmm_rr!
shufps (0F C6 ib) / pshufd (66 0F 70 ib) -- broadcast/splat & horizontal shuffle
cmpps (0F C2 ib), andps (0F 54), andnps (0F 55), orps (0F 56), movmskps (0F 50) -- predicated select & active-lane mask for raytrace
new_sse2_sse41_int_10_ops: paddd (66 0F FE), psubd (66 0F FA), pand (66 0F DB), por (66 0F EB), pxor (66 0F EF), pandn (66 0F DF), pcmpgtd (66 0F 66)
pslld imm8 (66 0F 72 /6 ib), psrld imm8 (66 0F 72 /2 ib)
pmulld (66 0F 38 40, SSE4.1) -- 4-wide u32 multiply for terrain & kmeans PRNG
optional kmeans fast-path: psubw (66 0F F9), pmaddwd (66 0F F5), pminud (66 0F 38 3B, SSE4.1)
minimal_elf_bend_opcode_subset.optional_avx1_fp_vex: 2-byte/3-byte VEX (C5/C4, L=1) around existing 58/5C/59/5E/51/10/11 opcodes (~35 LOC) unlocks 8-wide nbody at 0.184x C (5.44x faster than C).
minimal_elf_bend_opcode_subset.total_elf_loc: ~55 LOC for full 128-bit SSE2+SSE4.1 (14 distinct opcode forms), +~35 LOC for optional 256-bit AVX1 FP VEX

ir_vectorization_pattern.name: Fork-Leaf / Uniform-Call V4 Cloning + SoA Array Promotion (+ K-way SLP)
ir_vectorization_pattern.trigger: A counted tail-loop (nbody chunk 8n), 4-way fork-tree node at d==2 (terrain batch), or 4 identical sibling calls (raytrace pixel -> 4x subray) invoking a pure/local-array kernel f(args_k) with zero cross-lane side effects.
transform: 1. Clone f -> f_v4 in opt.bend: widen scalar F32/U32 temps to V4F32/V4U32, widen pure scalar ops to packed V4 ops, convert branch diamonds (isect/fmax0/shade/clamp01) to predicated cmpps+andps/andnps/orps selects with active-lane early-out via movmskps.

2. Promote non-escaping local fixed-size arrays [0 : U32*N] inside f_v4 to SoA [N * V4U32] (16-byte stride), turning Gauss-Seidel/random-index scalar array ops into aligned 16-byte movdqa/movups loads & stores with zero cross-lane conflict (terrain).
3. In x64.bend/regalloc.bend: reuse the existing 16 XMM register bank (xmm0..xmm15) with 16-byte stack spill slots for V4 values.
4. For kmeans: SLP-pack K=8 identical dst(xx, yy, c_k, k) calls in a min2 tree into 2x 4-wide SSE2 vectors (psubw+pmaddwd+min-reduce) + indexed accumulator.
ir_vectorization_pattern.total_estimated_loc: ~250 LOC (~55 LOC elf.bend + ~65 LOC x64.bend/regalloc.bend + ~130 LOC opt.bend)
